explanation: Akbar's workshop spent about 15 years painting it on cotton cloth in the 1560s and 1570s. Fewer than 200 of its pages survive, scattered among museums.

claims.text: The Hamzanama, illustrated with about 1,400 paintings, was made for the Mughal emperor Akbar.
The Hamzanama was not made for Shah Jahan, Aurangzeb or Babur.
Akbar's painting workshop worked on the Hamzanama for about 15 years, in the 1560s and 1570s.
The Hamzanama paintings were made on cotton cloth.
Fewer than 200 of the Hamzanama's paintings survive.

One writer WebSearch (Hamzanama Akbar 1,400 paintings cotton survive): the Victoria and Albert Museum, which holds pages (Tier A), gives 1,400 illustrations of which fewer than 200 survive, and The Art Newspaper agrees on 1,400 on cotton; other results put survivors nearer 100 to 140, all under 200.
